translations.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen sojourners of the dispersion in Pontus and Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and by the holiness of the Spirit, for obedience and for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. Grace to you, and may peace be multiplied!
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who by his great mercy has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for the salvation prepared to be revealed at the last time.
In this you now rejoice, though for a little while, if it must be, you have been distressed by trials of many kinds,
so that the testing of your faith, more precious than perishable gold that is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise and glory and honour at the revelation of Jesus Christ,
whom you did not know, yet you love him; whom you do not see now, yet you believe in him. Rejoice with a joy that is inexpressible and glorious.
And you will receive, at the end of your faith, the salvation of souls,
the salvation which the prophets searched out and inquired into, they who prophesied to you of the grace,
searching when, or at what time, the Spirit of Christ within them was making it known, when it testified to them beforehand about the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in the things that have now been announced to you by your evangelists through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things that the angels have longed to see.
Therefore gird up the loins of your minds, be watchful, and set your hope fully on that grace of theirs [?] which is coming at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not conform yourselves to the former desires of your ignorance,
but like the Holy One who called you, you also be holy in all your conduct.
For it is written: "Be holy, for I am holy."
And if you call on him as Father, who judges the deeds of each person without partiality, spend the time of your sojourning in fear.
Know that you were redeemed from the futile way of life handed down from your fathers not with perishable silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot,
who was foreknown before the creation of the world but was revealed in these last times for your sake;
through him you have come to believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope may be in God.
Purify your souls by obedience to the truth, through the Spirit; for brotherly love be without hypocrisy; with a pure heart love one another earnestly.
You have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the word of the living God, which abides forever.
For all flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is like the flower of grass: the grass withered, and its flower fell away.
But the word of God abides forever, and this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.
So put away all wickedness and all deceit and double-mindedness and envy and every kind of evil speech.
Like newborn infants, long for the spiritual milk that has no deceit in it, so that by it you may grow up to salvation,
if you have tasted that the Lord is sweet,
coming to him, the living stone, who was rejected by men but chosen and precious with God.
And you also, like chosen stones, are to be built up into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices that are pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is written in Scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will never be put to shame."
So the honour is for you who believe. But for the disobedient there is the stone that the builders rejected, which has become the head of the corner, and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence;
they stumble because they disobey the word, as they were appointed to do.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy seed, a people acquired by God, so that you may declare the virtues of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God. Once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you as strangers and sojourners to keep away from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul.
Keep your conduct among the Gentiles good, so that where they speak evil of you as evildoers, they may be put to shame by your good works and glorify God on the day of visitation.
So submit yourselves to every human creature for the Lord's sake: whether to the king, since he is over all,
or to governors, as those sent by him to punish evildoers and to praise those who do good.
For this is the will of God: that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a cover for wickedness; live as servants of God.
Honour everyone, love the brothers, fear God, honour the king.
Servants, submit to your own masters with all fear, not only to those who are good and gentle but also to those who are harsh.
For this is grace from God: when someone, with a good mind toward God, endures sorrows while suffering unjustly.
For how is it better if you sin, are beaten for it, and endure it? But if you do good and suffer for it and endure it, this is grace from God.
You were appointed for this very thing, because Christ also suffered for us and left you an example, so that you would follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.
When he was reviled, he reviled no one in return. When he suffered, he threatened no one. The Righteous One handed himself over to the judge.
He carried our sins in his own body on the cross, so that we might leave sin behind and live in righteousness. By his wounds we were healed.
For you were like sheep gone astray, but now you have turned back to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
Likewise, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if some are disobedient to the word, they may be won without a word by the conduct of the wives,
when they see your holy conduct in fear,
whose adornment should not be the outward braiding of hair and the putting on of gold, or the wearing of clothing,
but the hidden person of the heart, with the incorruptible manner of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
For in this way the holy women of old, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves and were subject to their own husbands,
just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. You have become her children by doing good and not being afraid of any fear.
Likewise, husbands, live together with them with forbearance, as with the weaker vessel. Give honour to the women as fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayer may not be hindered.
Finally, all of you be of one mind, merciful, loving the brethren, forbearing, humble.
Do not repay evil for evil, or insult for insult, but bless the one who opposes you, and know that you were appointed for this very purpose, so that you may inherit a blessing.
For whoever wants to love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil, and let his lips not speak deceit;
let him turn away from evil and do good, let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are open to their prayer, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.
And who is there who will do you evil if you become imitators of what is good?
And even if you suffer for the sake of righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be troubled.
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope that is among you, with gentleness and fear.
Keep a good conscience, so that those who speak evil of you as of evildoers, those who abuse your good conduct in Christ, may be put to shame.
For it is better, if God's will should decree your suffering, that you suffer while doing good than while doing evil.
For Christ also suffered once for our sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that he might bring us to God. He died in the flesh and was made alive in the spirit,
in which he also went to the prison of the spirits and preached
to those who were once disobedient, when the long-suffering of God waited once in the days of Noah, during the preparation of the ark, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved from the water.
In the likeness of this, baptism now saves you too: not the removal of filth from the flesh, but the longing of a good mind toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, who ascended into heaven, and angels, authorities and powers were made subject to him.
Since Christ suffered in the flesh for us, arm yourselves also with the same mind, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
so that you may live the rest of your time in the flesh no longer by human desires but by the will of God.

For the time of this life that has already passed is enough for us to have done the will of the Gentiles, who walk in the impurity of desires, in drunkenness, revelling, carousing and lawless idolatry.
They are surprised that you do not join them in the same flood of impurity, and they revile you.
They will give an account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this is why the gospel was preached to the dead: so that they might be judged in the flesh as humans are, but live in the spirit through God.
The end of all things has come near. So purify yourselves and stay alert for prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another intense, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
Each of you should use the gift you have received to serve one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

Whoever speaks should speak as one speaking the words of God. Whoever serves should serve with the strength that God gives, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not think it strange that this fiery ordeal has come among you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice to the extent that you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also rejoice and be glad when his glory is revealed.
If you are loved [?] for the name of Christ, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you. In their view you are reviled, but in your view you are glorified.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as one who meddles in other people's affairs.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this lot.
For the time has come for judgment to begin, and it will begin first with the house of God. If it begins first with us, what will become of those who disobey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous person is barely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner be found?
Therefore, let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good.
I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a sharer in the glory that is to be revealed: shepherd the flock of God that is among you,
caring for it not under compulsion but willingly, as God wants, and not for shameful gain but eagerly.
Do not lord it over the portion entrusted to you, but be examples to the flock.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
In the same way, you young men, be subject to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility in submission to one another, for God crushes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you in his own time.
Cast all your care upon him, for he cares for you.
Be watchful, be vigilant, for your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to swallow up.
Resist him, steadfast in the faith,
and the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory through Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, will himself strengthen you, establish you, empower you, and make you firm.
To him be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, your faithful brother, as I regard him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting you and testifying that this is the true grace of God, in which you stand.
Greetings to you from the one who is in Babylon, together with the elect, and from Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with you, all who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
